subject: Media Literacy
title: Pamphlets and the Reformation
description: One-minute skill: Pamphlets and the Reformation.

hook.text: Martin Luther nailed 95 theses to a church door. The printing press made sure the world heard.

buildup.text: Within two weeks, copies of Luther's arguments were circulating across Germany.

discovery.text: Pamphlets became the social media of the 1500s — cheap, fast, and impossible to suppress.

twist.text: Luther wrote in German, not Latin, so ordinary people could read his ideas. Language was strategy.

climax.text: The Reformation proved that cheap print media could topple institutions that had lasted a millennium.

punchline.text: The Church had power. Luther had a printer.

quiz.question: Why did Luther write in German instead of Latin?
options: So ordinary people could read his ideas
German was the official church language
